Uncontested divorce: the steps and what to prepare

How an uncontested divorce works before a notary, which conditions apply and which documents you need.

By Eleni Nikolaou14 September 20264 min read

Since 2018 an uncontested divorce in Greece no longer needs a court. It is done by notarial deed, provided both spouses agree to end the marriage and the marriage has lasted at least six months.

The steps

  1. Each spouse chooses their own lawyer.
  2. The lawyers draft the written divorce agreement and, if there are minor children, the agreement on custody and contact.
  3. The agreement is filed with the notary, together with the spouses' statement that they still wish to divorce, after a ten-day reflection period.
  4. The notary draws up the deed, which is then entered in the civil registry.

What to prepare

  • Marriage certificate
  • Family status certificate
  • ID cards and tax numbers (AFM)
  • If you have children, a first idea of their day-to-day life: where they will live, how contact will work, what maintenance will be paid

How long it takes

Once the agreement is ready and the documents are complete, the process usually finishes within a few weeks. Most of the time goes into the spouses reaching agreement, not into the formalities.

This article is general information and is not legal advice for your situation. The law changes: check the publication date.
